summary:
The first review holds up on everything grounded in measurement. B1 is a real blocker. The design sends every pre-scan observation through the kind of handle open that SL-045 measured refreshing stale directory entries. It also credits that refresh to directory listing, which is the opposite of what was measured. As a result the criterion 1, 3 and 7 tests would pass against the unchanged IsDue code. M1, M3, M4, M6 and M7 are correct at major.

Three findings are graded too high. M2 and M8 protect against future drift, not a defect in the design as written, and HeldOpenTreeTests already checks criterion 6 end to end. M5 only sharpens a drive-time estimate that the design already treats as advisory and already re-measures at validate. m7 is suspicious: the criterion 6 before/after comparison of every temp-tree folder already catches a marshaling slip, and the reviewer says they could not confirm the Controlled Folder Access half.

The whole approach is sound. U-005 and U-018 force probing every file. But the reviews missed one structural point. The overlapped bounded pipeline exists to beat a 150 s bar that the design calls advisory. The measured sequential shape was 188.3 s: list everything on one thread, then probe every file with 16 workers. It would remove most of the risk behind M2, M3 and M4, yet it was only ever named as a fallback. The design also contradicts itself on what a missed time bar means.

Two smaller gaps were also missed:
- Nobody measured probe-all on network volumes, where every file costs its own round trips.
- The design never says what path form the probe uses now that every name goes through it.

assessments.note: Blocker is the right level: criterion 1 is the slice's main behaviour, and its test would pass against the unchanged IsDue. The design makes it worse. HeldOpenTreeTests says 'a listing itself was measured ... to refresh stale entries' and then observes only through HoldRig's handle-based snapshot. SL-045 measured the opposite: the metadata open refreshes the entry. So the design's observation rule moves observation onto the very operation that causes the problem. One addition to fix (1): 'never open held files from a third process' has to cover implicit opens in the test process too. File.Exists or FileInfo.Length on grow.bin/locked.bin go through GetFileAttributesEx/NtQueryFullAttributesFile, which opens the file internally, so they can refresh the entry in the same way.

Major is right. The contradiction reaches criterion 1 as well as criterion 6. Criterion 1's own check ('the listing must be shown to still say 0 B' while the helper holds the file) cannot hold after the scan, because the scan's probe refreshes the entry (SL-045). This is an agreed criterion contradicted by a measurement, so it has to be reported and interpreted on the record. The design settles it quietly by choosing which observer to use.

As written, the design is single-writer. The ProbePipeline contract has Drain/Complete called by the listing thread, apply runs on the caller's thread, and workers never receive the apply delegate. Every failure scenario the finding gives needs a future change that breaks that contract. The reviewer is right that rule 1 fences a call ProbePipeline has no reason to make, and a thread-affinity assert is a cheap fix. But this is protection against future drift, not a defect.

Correct and concrete. Nothing passes a token to Submit, so cancelling while the 8192-slot queue is full leaves the listing thread blocked forever, before it reaches the Drain that would rethrow a fault. StallRig is exactly the scenario that fills the queue. Complete's applied != submitted check also turns an ordinary cancel into an invariant failure.

Major is right. Under probe-all the inline repeat probe is redundant: U-010 shows the handle query is exact through any name. It sits on the critical path, and it forces a material race case that ProbePipeline gives no deterministic way to test. One part of the finding misreads the design. 'Fallback lever if drive time regresses' most likely means that if eligibility is later narrowed to save time, the repeat path still protects criterion 4. That rationale is not backwards, though it does not justify keeping the probe in this design.

The design already calls the overlap bet unmeasured, puts it in decidable_disagreements, and schedules a validate re-measurement of the built, pipelined Scanner.Scan. That measurement would include every omitted item on the listing thread: fallback double-opens, the SetFileInformationByHandle calls, inline probes and drains. The finding improves the estimate and adds a worker-priority tweak. Neither affects correctness or any of the 7 criteria. The UI starvation point is plausible but has no measurement behind it.

Major is right. This is the scanner's first write-class operation, and it is applied to every folder, including sync roots, SMB, FAT/exFAT and ReFS. It was measured only on local NTFS %TEMP%. One addition to the re-spike in the fix: also watch the parent with ReadDirectoryChangesW during the suppressed listing. An unchanged USN does not prove that no change notification reached OneDrive, the indexer or other watchers.

Major is right. For a non-admin user, fallback is a large share of real folders (Windows, Program Files, WinSxS), and no temp-tree folder ever takes that path. The contract wording '(and recorded as unreadable) exactly as today' really can be read as marking fallback folders unreadable, and every existing test would still pass under that reading.

Criterion 6 is enforced by HeldOpenTreeTests diffing every entry after a real Scanner.Scan, so a timestamp write anywhere on the scan path turns it red. Rule 2 is a secondary fence against future drift. The Kernel32.cs declaration tripping the rule is real build friction, but a one-line except_files entry fixes it. The unfenced APIs and a second listing outside DirectoryReader are both future-code risks.

The build-check cited only the deny-fixture lines. The test's name implies it asserts that a non-WOF, zero-allocation file is not probed, and Probes counts will change either way. 'Rename only' is not supported.
Right. Once every probed file carries SizeProbed, 'the probe changed the figure' has no signal left, and B1 fix (4) depends on that signal.

Right on both counts. The criterion-5 test asserts ProbeFailed and ProbeFailures==1, so a switch to NtOpenFile would turn it red, not slip past silently. The rule also fences only one of the files where that switch is likely.

The concern depends on how SynchronousIoCancel binds to a thread, and the reviewer did not read the constructor. Still, 'each worker has its own instance' does not say where the instance is built, and checking is cheap. Minor fits.

The 8192-deep queue widens the gap between listing and probing from microseconds to potentially seconds. In that gap, deleted files get counted with ACL refusals, and a replaced path can apply the new file's size to the old entry. Minor fits.
The rule for criterion 7's expected total for the hardlinked file depends on first-seen order. With both names in one folder, per-folder attribution is never tested.

The design's own criterion-6 case covers the marshaling slip. HeldOpenTreeTests diffs all four timestamps and the attributes of every temp-tree entry after a scan in which every folder takes the suppressed-open path, because the user owns them all. A wrong FILE_BASIC_INFO layout would change a timestamp or an attribute there and fail the test. The reviewer states that the Controlled Folder Access half is unverified, so it is too speculative to act on beyond recording CFA state, which costs nothing.
The citations do overreach: 'or a threshold is crossed', the SO asker's impression presented as a finding, and a content-farm URL. As the reviewer says, none of them carries weight in the design.

missed.claim: The overlapped bounded pipeline exists only to chase a 150 s bar that the design itself calls advisory. The measured sequential shape was never considered as the primary design: a single-threaded listing walk, then dedicated workers probing every eligible entry, then all results applied on the listing thread after the workers join. It came in at 188.3 s. It removes the Submit backpressure deadlock behind M3. It makes single-writer structural, because apply happens only after the join (M2). It makes the inline-versus-async ordering in M4 deterministic. The design also contradicts itself on what a time miss means: key_decisions calls the drive-time re-measurement 'advisory only', while decidable_disagreements marks the same question would_force_resynthesis: true. If validate measures above 150 s, nothing says whether the slice passes or goes back to design.
missed.evidence: probe-all-as-built-route-drive-time: 'Warm listing+as-built-probe-all took 188.3s (100.7 list + 87.6 probe)' (sequential, measured). ProbePipeline contract: 'Submit(entry,path) blocks past capacity'. key_decisions: 'The validate-stage drive-time re-measurement ... is advisory, not a done-when gate'. decidable_disagreements[0].would_force_resynthesis: true. None of the 7 criteria names a time budget. M5's fix (3) names the sequential shape only as a fallback.
missed.fix: Make the two-phase shape the baseline. During the walk the listing thread records the index of each eligible entry. After the walk, dedicated workers probe by index into a results array, building paths from the store's parent chain, which nothing writes during this phase, instead of holding about 3.5M path strings. The listing thread then applies every result after the join. The design record should state the costs: files keep their listing figures until the probe phase ends (a tail of about 90 s), and progress reporting needs a 'sizing' phase. Keep the overlap as a later optimisation, adopted only after measurement and only if a person makes time a done-when criterion. Either way, remove the advisory-versus-resynthesis contradiction.

missed.claim: Probe-all adds at least one create/query/close round trip per file on network volumes. Nothing measured this. The only drive-time evidence is local NVMe C:, and the validate re-measurement is on C: only. The old rule probed a handful of files per share. The eligibility rule has no condition on volume type, so an SMB share with a million files over a few-millisecond link can easily pay more for probing than for listing. The first place anyone would see that is in use.
missed.evidence: probe-all-as-built-route-drive-time touched 'real C:\ (NTFS, 994 GB, NVMe SSD)'. The 'Drive-time re-measurement' contract repeats that method on C:. SizeProbe eligibility rule: 'ordinary file && !link && !cloudOnly && first name', with no volume condition. The project has an SMB loopback rig and StallRig, so SMB volumes are in scope.
missed.fix: Record the per-file round-trip cost on network volumes in the design record. Extend the validate re-measurement to the loopback SMB rig and report per-probe latency and total probe time next to the listing time. The time is advisory, so if the ratio is large, put it to a person rather than finding out in the field.

missed.claim: The probe now opens every name by path through an unchanged SizeProbe.Probe. Before this slice it only reached files of 64 MiB or more, WOF suspects and repeat names, so the existing long-path fixture from SL-020 and any unusual-name fixtures probably never exercised it. If the path is not \\?\-prefixed, a path over MAX_PATH fails to open and the file keeps its stale listing figure, counted as ProbeFailed and never flagged. A name with a trailing dot or space ('a.') is normalised to a different name, so it can be sized as another file. That is the silent mis-sizing this slice exists to remove. The design never states the path form the probe receives.
missed.evidence: Probe-set rule: 'SizeProbe.Probe itself is unchanged'. Build-check: IsDue 'Runs in three cases only'. Q-002 decision: SL-020 needed a real-tree test for long paths. Scanner.Correct keeps the listing figure on any nonzero probe error.
missed.fix: State in the design that probes receive \\?\-prefixed full paths, after checking what SizeProbe is given today. In the existing long-path test, assert that the entry is SizeProbed and that ProbeFailures is 0. Add a fixture file named with a trailing dot, created through a \\?\ path, and assert that it is charged at its own handle-reported size.

payload.notes: The reviewer is strongest when a finding traces to a recorded measurement. B1, M1, M3, M6 and M7 each cite a spike or an earlier slice's result, and each holds up. B1 caught something the design's own wording hides: it credits the entry refresh to listing when SL-045 measured the handle open doing it. The inflation is in findings that harden against future drift (M2 and M8, both major for fences against later code) and in findings that sharpen an estimate the design already calls advisory and re-measures (M5). m7 mixes a slip the criterion-6 test already catches with a Controlled Folder Access claim the reviewer could not verify. The reviewer misread one rationale in M4 ('fallback lever'), though the rest of that finding stands. The reviewer named the measured sequential shape but only as a fallback, and never asked whether the overlap is worth its failure surface when the time bar is advisory. That question is the main thing this pass adds.
